item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-10 12:00
Institution: Politecnico MILANO, Milan
Field: Civil engineering and architecture / 08/CEAR-04 Geomatica

Satellite Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (InSAR) enables monitoring of nonlinear ground deformation with millimetre-level precision and high spatial and temporal resolution. It supports the observation of natural and anthropogenic assets, where slow ground motion may accumulate and lead to subsidence, slope failures, and structural damage. This research addresses the shift from measurement to interpretation and action through: (1) consolidation of InSAR processing schemes; (2) fusion of InSAR products with external data sources across multiple spatial scales; and (3) translation of interpreted deformation into a risk context, enabling retrospective and multi-scenario anticipatory…

The research concerns the design, methodological coordination, and psychometric and statistical validation of tools for the assessment and certification of proficiency in Italian Sign Language (LIS). item.title: Contratto di ricerca: Characterization of the transmission dynamics of Xylella fastidiosa by insect vectors in vineyards and semi-natural environments (Univ. BARI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-20 23:55
Institution: Univ. BARI, Lussemburgo
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-05 Patologia vegetale ed entomologia

*Xylella fastidiosa* subsp. *fastidiosa* Sequence Type 1 (Xff-ST1) represents a new threat to European viticulture, particularly in light of its detection in table grape vineyards in Apulia. The project aims to understand the epidemiology of *Xylella fastidiosa* in table grape vineyards and to investigate the role of spontaneous vegetation and non-cultivated environments in supporting insect vector populations and acting as sources or recipients of the bacterium. The results will improve the understanding of vector-pathogen-host interactions, identify key epidemiological risk factors, and provide data useful for risk assessment and the development of effective disease management strategies.

In 2012 Fyodorov, Hiary, and Keating formulated a striking conjecture: the maxima of log-determinants of large random matrices behave like those of logarithmically correlated fields. While there has been huge progress in proving this conjecture, most of the current results are for integrable models.
